text:
If your Saturday plan was built around sunshine, Burlington’s running a little behind schedule: it’s cloudy and 68 so far, with a north wind around 10 mph. The afternoon should brighten at times, but a shower is possible after 2, and the forecast models are split, with the Euro much wetter than the others. I’d still bet on a mostly dry afternoon, but keep a rain jacket nearby. North winds will strengthen on the lake, pushing waves up to 1 to 3 feet, so this is a better shoreline day than an open-water outing.

Clouds break up tonight, with a low near 52 and the north wind easing some. Sunday looks like the cleaner bet, sunny and near 73, though the lake stays choppy with north winds of 15 to 20 knots early. Plan outdoor time this afternoon, but don’t commit to a long boat ride, and expect a cool, breezy evening.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): Labor Day will be another beautiful day with mostly sunny skies and highs in the mid-70s. Lows will be in the 50s. Tuesday will also be dry and decent. The next chance for rain will be Wednesday. It could be a soaker, but significant weather isn’t expected. This will be followed by the coolest air of the season so far for the end of the week. Thursday will be partly sunny with the chance for showers. Highs will be in the 60s. Isolated frost can’t be ruled out Thursday night into Friday morning for the Adirondacks and Northeast Kingdom, so stay tuned for updates. Friday will be a fall preview with partly sunny skies and highs only in the upper 50s to low 60s. Keep the jackets handy if you’re out during the evenings.
